level-1.title: Ways people earn
summary: A salary is a fixed amount paid every month.
A wage is paid for each hour or each day of work.
A business owner earns profit. Profit is sales minus costs.
Skills raise your pay. A skilled worker is paid more than an untrained one.
Deaf adults work in every field, including design, teaching, and computers.

questions.prompt: One worker is paid the same ₹15,000 every month no matter how many days they work. Another is paid ₹500 for each day they show up. Which one earns a salary, and which a wage?

image.alt: A fixed monthly payslip beside a daily wage counter

options.label: The first earns a salary; the second earns a wage

questions.hint: A salary does not change with the number of days worked; a wage does.

questions.prompt: You sell handmade cards for ₹40 each. You sell 20 cards. Your total costs for materials were ₹300. What is your profit?

image.alt: A stall of handmade cards with a cost sheet

questions.hint: First find total sales, then subtract the total costs.

questions.prompt: Two drivers apply for the same job. One has a special licence for driving large trucks; the other does not. Who is more likely to be offered higher pay, and why?

image.alt: A special driving licence beside an ordinary one

options.label: Neither - pay never depends on skills
The one with the special licence - skills raise how much you are paid
The one without the licence, since they are cheaper to hire

questions.hint: Recall what the lesson says about skilled versus untrained workers.

level-2.title: Earning, taxes and take-home pay
summary: Gross pay is the full amount you earn. Net pay is what reaches your account.
The difference is deductions, such as income tax and provident fund.
Tax money pays for roads, hospitals and government schools.
Freelance work has no fixed salary. You are paid per project.
Always ask for the net amount before accepting a job.

questions.prompt: Your gross pay is ₹25,000. Income tax takes ₹2,000 and provident fund takes ₹1,500. What is your net pay?

image.alt: A payslip showing gross pay and two separate deductions

questions.hint: Subtract both deductions from the gross pay, not just one.

questions.prompt: A job offer says 'salary ₹30,000.' You do not ask whether that is gross or net. Why could this cause a problem later?

image.alt: A job offer letter with an unclear pay figure

options.label: The actual amount reaching your account could be noticeably less than ₹30,000 after deductions
Net and gross are always the same number
There is no possible problem, ₹30,000 always means ₹30,000

questions.hint: Recall the difference between the number an offer states and the number that actually lands in an account.

questions.prompt: A salaried worker gets the same ₹20,000 every month. A freelancer earns ₹35,000 one month and ₹5,000 the next, depending on projects. What is the key difference in what each can rely on?

image.alt: A steady salary line beside an up-and-down freelance income line

options.label: The salaried worker has a predictable amount each month; the freelancer's income varies and is less certain
There is no real difference between the two
The freelancer always earns more overall

questions.hint: Think about which one you could plan a fixed monthly budget around more easily.

level-3.title: How tax works, and what a job really pays
summary: Income tax in India is charged in slabs. Each slice of income has its own rate, and the rates rise as income rises.
A higher rate applies only to the slice above the line, not to all your income. Moving into a new slab never leaves you with less.
Your average tax rate is total tax divided by total income. It is always lower than the rate on your top slab.
Provident fund (PF) keeps back part of your salary, and your employer adds its own share. It is saving you get later, not money lost.
A job’s real value is salary plus benefits - PF, health insurance, paid leave. Compare these, not just the salary number.
Freelancers and gig workers must set aside their own tax, because no employer takes it out for them.

questions.prompt: In a made-up tax system, the first ₹3 lakh is taxed at 0% and everything above it at 10%. Riya earns ₹5 lakh. How much tax does she pay?

image.alt: Income split into two slices, with different rates

questions.hint: Only the part above ₹3 lakh is taxed at 10%.

questions.prompt: A friend says: "Don’t take the raise - it will push you into a higher slab and you’ll take home less." Is this true?

image.alt: Two people talking about a pay rise

options.label: No - only the extra slice is taxed higher, so you still take home more
Yes - all your income gets the higher rate

questions.hint: Remember which part of your income a higher slab applies to.

questions.prompt: Job A pays ₹25,000 with no PF or health cover. Job B pays ₹23,000 plus PF and health insurance for your family. What is the best way to compare them?

image.alt: Two job offers side by side

options.label: Pick Job A, because the salary is higher
Pick Job B, because the salary is lower
Add up salary and benefits, then compare the full value

questions.hint: A job pays you in more ways than the salary number.
